title: Handle rolling-deployment client/server version skew
businessContext: An old tab submits an action after the serving deployment has changed and the team assumes every payload is interchangeable.
problemStatement: Design the system for Long-lived browser tabs while deployments roll across 20 instances. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: Long-lived browser tabs while deployments roll across 20 instances
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Keep immutable build assets available for their supported client lifetime and use the deployment platform’s supported version-skew/affinity strategy where available.
The CDN may retain an old HTML document while its referenced chunks are deleted. Retain assets through the support window, coordinate cache headers and verify that rollback assets remain fetchable.
alternativeApproaches: Reload is a recovery option, not a consistency protocol. Preserve drafts where appropriate, detect incompatibility before repeating writes and retain old assets while managing application/API compatibility.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Open a tab on release A, roll to B, then navigate and mutate.
Test mixed instances and a partial deployment rollback.
Verify chunk availability, action error handling and mutation idempotency under skew.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
